newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Major to visit Bangladesh, Pakistan in turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Major to visit Bangladesh, Pakistan in turmoil.

text.p: Britain's Prime Minister John Major will visit Bangladesh and Pakistan, both in political turmoil, as part of a South Asian tour to promote British trade and investment.
Major, now in India, meets Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday only two days after former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad's release from six years in jail.

Ershad, welcomed joyously by supporters after he was granted bail on the last of 17 corruption charges, vowed to re-enter politics, denying opposition charges that he had been freed after a deal between his Jatiya Party and Hasina's Awami League.
The British premier, who faces a general election within four months, flies on to Pakistan, where elections are just over three weeks away, on Sunday for talks with caretaker premier Meraj Khalid.
On Monday Major will meet President Farooq Leghari, who used controversial powers to sack Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
He was also due to hold separate meetings with Bhutto and her main political rival Nawaz Sharif, whose Pakistan Muslim League is widely tipped to win the February 3 election.
The visits to the two Islamic countries coincide with the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, when the pace of political and business activity normally slackens.
"The timing is not perfect," a British diplomat in Islamabad said. "But this is a good chance to show that we are not fair weather friends and there is still business we can do."
Major's visits to Pakistan and India form part of a series of events to mark their 50 years of independence from Britain.
In Dhaka, Hasina and Major will be discussing prospects for British investment and ways to develop trade, now tilted towards Bangladesh thanks to its vibrant ready-made garments industry.

Bangladesh's exports to Britain totalled 239 million pounds ($406 million) in the first nine months of 1996, compared to imports worth 59 million pounds. "Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will pursue more British investment, particularly in gas exploration and power generation," a foreign ministry official said.

Hasina and Major, the first British premier to visit Bangladesh since former Labour leader James Callaghan in 1978, are expected to witness the signing of a deal between Britain's Cairns Energy Plc and Petrobangla, the state-run oil and gas exploration agency, for development of an offshore gas field.
Cairns has already spent $30 million on exploration in the Bay of Bengal, 35 km (22 miles) southwest of Chittagong Port.

Major, whose country gives Bangladesh more than 56 million pounds a year to make it Dhaka's second biggest aid donor, will visit a British-aided poverty alleviation project near the capital before leaving for Islamabad on Sunday.
A Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman said Khalid's talks with Major would cover Afghanistan, the Kashmir dispute with India and the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation.
"Major will preach the need for Indian-Pakistani talks, especially on trade liberalisation, which we see as a good way of getting a dialogue going," a British diplomat said.

Major was expected to voice hopes that February 3 polls would go ahead according to the constitution and stress the need for consistent economic policy-making and respect for contracts as a sound basis for foreign investment, the diplomat said.
He might also push for the removal of delays to several major projects in Pakistan in which British firms have interests.

These include a power transmission scheme by National Grid Company Ltd, a planned $450 million PTA (pure terephthalic acid) plant to be built by ICI Pakistan Ltd near Karachi, and the Lahore airport expansion involving Siemens-Plessey.

Major is accompanied by at least 30 top British business executives who will hold a seminar with their counterparts in Lahore on Tuesday. British exports to Pakistan were worth 340 million pounds in 1995 against imports worth 363 million pounds.
($1.7 = one pound)
